title: Japan’s 2026 Defense White Paper Warns of China’s Expanding Military Reach in the Pacific
author: Takahashi Kosuke
text:
The Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force’s second Izumo-class helicopter carrier Kaga, whose bow has been modified to a rectangular shape to enable operations of the stealth F-35B fighter.
Credit: Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force
On August 4, Japan’s Cabinet approved the 2026 edition of its annual defense white paper, warning that China is steadily expanding its military reach into the Pacific beyond the First Island Chain, the strategic arc linking Japan’s southwestern islands, Taiwan, and the Philippines. The report, Defense of Japan 2026, again described China as “an unprecedented and the greatest strategic challenge” to Japan’s peace and security, repeating language first adopted in Japan’s revised National Security Strategy in 2022. This year’s white paper placed particular emphasis on China’s expanding military activities in the Pacific, highlighting what Tokyo views as Beijing’s growing ability to project military power beyond the so-called First Island Chain and increasingly deeper into the Pacific.[...]
